texts.facts: Further, they voluntarily caused hurt to child namely Raju Mehto and thereby, committed an offence punishable under Section 23 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, and Section 323 IPC, for which FIR no.416/2014 was registered at the police station Dwarka Sector 23, New Delhi. After registration of the FIR, the Investigating Officer (hereinafter, "IO") undertook investigation and on culmination of the same, the chargesheet against the accused persons was filed. The Ld. Predecessor of this court took the cognizance against the accused person Amit Verma and summons were issued to the accused person. On their appearance, copy of the chargesheet was supplied to the accused in terms of section 207 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter, "CrPC"). On finding a prima facie case against the accused Amit Verma, notice under Section 23 of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of FIR No.416/2014, PS Dwarka Sector 23 State vs. Amit Verma anr. Page 2 of 23 Abhinav Ahlawat Date: Ahlawat 2024.03.01 15:58:24 +0530 Children) Act, and Section 323 IPC was framed against accused Amit Verma on 23.02.2022. Upon the supply of chargesheet, notice U/s 23 of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, and Section 323 IPC was framed against accused Binny Verma on 19.05.2022. The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. He did not serve any notice upon the public persons who refused to join the proceedings. He did not record any statement of family members of the child victim as nobody from the family of the child victim ever met him when the matter remained with him for investigation. He had not served any notice upon the family members of the child victim to join the investigation.

30. The words used in section 23 JJ Act is wilful neglect, meaning thereby neglecting a child wilfully is a grave injustice that inflict unnecessary suffering upon the most vulnerable member of our society.
Every child deserves to grow up in an environment filled with love, care and support.
Such neglect deprives the child not only of essential nurturing and guidance but also undermines their sense of security and self-worth.
It is imperative that we as a society recognise and address instances of wilful neglect promptly and effectively.
In the instant case, it is evident from the testimony of the child PW1 that he was made to do the household work although he was sent for some other purposes.
Instances of beating were stated by the child which created a sense of fear in him which ultimately led him to leave the house.
This is nothing but wilfully creating a hostile environment for child who was living without his mother in a house send for giving him a sense of comfort and security.
